title: Canadian C-spine rule
subtitle: Cervical-spine imaging after blunt trauma
summary: Uses high-risk factors, low-risk factors and active neck rotation to determine whether cervical-spine imaging is indicated.
population: Alert, stable patients after blunt trauma where cervical-spine injury is being considered.
exclusions: Use only within local trauma and spinal-motion-restriction policy.

May be inappropriate with altered mental state, unreliable intoxication assessment, neurological deficit, haemodynamic instability, penetrating trauma, communication barriers or significant spinal disease.

criteria.label: Dangerous mechanism
criteria.description: Examples: fall over 1 metre or 5 stairs; axial load to head; high-speed collision, rollover or ejection; motorised recreational vehicle; bicycle collision.

criteria.label: Paraesthesia in the upper or lower limbs
Simple rear-end collision
criteria.description: Not pushed into traffic, hit by a bus/large vehicle, rollover, or hit by a high-speed vehicle.

criteria.label: Ambulatory at any time since injury
Actively rotates neck 45° left and 45° right
criteria.description: Only assess after no high-risk factor and at least one low-risk factor.

results.label: Imaging not indicated
interpretation: Able to rotate 45° left and right after meeting low-risk criteria: imaging is not indicated by the Canadian C-spine rule.

results.label: Imaging indicated
interpretation: A high-risk factor, absence of a low-risk factor, or inability to rotate 45° indicates imaging.

overrides: Stop range-of-motion assessment if pain, neurological symptoms or clinician concern develops.
limitations: This is a branching decision rule rather than a simple summed score.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Formal clinical verification has not yet been recorded. Population, exclusions, thresholds, calculations, wording and implementation tests must be checked against the cited source.
